reality_delta: LS-006 claims convergence to closed_external_sample_verified, but the sample was generated by RedCap's own real-sample-generate and uses task_id=fixture-task — a name that is internally contradictory: evidence meant to prove "real external" explicitly announces "test fixture." Being placed outside the source tree (/Users/norven/workspace/redcap-e2e-runs/) does not make it an independent external project; it remains an artifact produced by the same tool invocation as the verification. The real gap — validating an independently existing external project that RedCap's toolchain did not create — remains unbridged.
main_concern: task_id=fixture-task semantically labels the sample as a test fixture. A real external project has meaningful identifiers from its own domain (issue numbers, task keys, project slugs), not a name that announces its manufactured nature. The real-sample-generate command proves the generator works, but does not prove Loom can discover, connect to, and validate a real external project that RedCap did not itself generate.
top_risks: Self-referential loop: real-sample-generate creates a sample -> real-sample-check --require-verified checks that sample -> task_id mismatch, checks fail -> task_id corrected to fixture-task, checks pass. This is not a verification fix; it is rotating the reference frame to align with the fixture. The system validates what it generated, every time.

Classification inflation: Marking a fixture-passing-verification as closed_external_sample_verified creates a false sense of completion in the ledger. A downstream agent or reviewer seeing this status will assume real project samples have been proven and may make further decisions on that basis. This risk is amplified because this task sits in an open repair queue — the queue consumes false completion signals.

Silent downgrade: The constraint says don't downgrade, but the task_id fix narrative — replacing a wrong task_id with fixture-task — presents as command correction. However fixture-task is not a real project identifier; it is a generator-assigned label. The actual downgrade: substituting real external proof with fixture generation while framing the change as error correction.
missing_evidence: A sample whose task_id independently belongs to an external project that exists outside RedCap (without fixture, test, or sample in the name), with its own domain context.
Evidence that the external sample and its chosen tasks existed before the real-sample-check run — i.e., not manufactured on demand during the same session as the generator to pass checks.

A demonstration that RedCap's verification can discover and successfully connect to an already-existing project without real-sample-generate having created that project's skeleton. This requires at minimum: given a known real external project path, automatic task_id discovery rather than passing a fixture task_id on the command line.
minimum_fix: Decouple the fixture from real external verification. Either: (a) Replace fixture-task with a real external project identifier — one that exists independently of the RedCap repo and generator output, and existed before the real-sample-check run; or (b) Roll back LS-006 status to open_solution_designed_no_fix with an honest note: "Generator verified (generate+check loop works against self-produced samples), but not yet proven against real external projects." In either case, rename fixture-task to something that indicates it is a generated fixture (e.g., generated-loom-sample-task) so that its artificial nature is immediately apparent to anyone reading the identifier in any context.

anti_loop_signal.reason: Pattern: generate fixture -> run checks against it -> fail due to task_id mismatch -> correct task_id to the one embedded in the fixture -> declare pass. This is not verifying external reality; it is adjusting inputs to make outputs match. A self-referential loop exists in external sample verification where the artifact being validated was created by the same tool doing the validation, and the error being fixed is using the correct task_id from the generation step.
